title: The Great Commission
summary: Jesus sent His followers to make disciples of all nations. Jesus sends His followers to make disciples and promises to be with them. When kids wonder if faith is only private, the Great Commission shows that good news is meant to be shared.

read_it.prompt: Read Matthew 28:16-20 like a scene you could retell: who is there, what happens, and what changes?

tell_it: After rising from the dead, Jesus sent His disciples to teach and baptize all nations. He promised His presence. Kids can retell it by naming what happened, who responded, and what God showed.
understand_it: The Great Commission should not be flattened into a slogan. Jesus sends His followers to make disciples and promises to be with them. When kids wonder if faith is only private, the Great Commission shows that good news is meant to be shared.
age_5_7_explanation: Jesus sent His followers to make disciples of all nations.
age_8_11_explanation: Jesus sends His followers to make disciples and promises to be with them. The lesson helps older kids compare the story's wise path with the easier path people may have wanted.
teen_explanation: When kids wonder if faith is only private, the Great Commission shows that good news is meant to be shared. Jesus sends His followers to make disciples and promises to be with them. The story leaves room to talk about courage, humility, repentance, or hope without pretending the hard part is small.
key_truths: Jesus sends His followers to make disciples and promises to be with them.
The Great Commission shows mission through a real Bible moment, not a slogan.
When kids wonder if faith is only private, the Great Commission shows that good news is meant to be shared.
life_application: When kids wonder if faith is only private, the Great Commission shows that good news is meant to be shared.

quiz_questions.question: What did Jesus promise His disciples?
choices: The mission was only for one town
quiz_questions.explanation: This answer keeps the focus where the Bible puts it: I am with you always. Jesus sends His followers to make disciples and promises to be with them.

quiz_questions.question: Which response best fits the lesson's point?
choices: Pretend the hard part in The Great Commission is not hard.
Use The Great Commission only to win a trivia point.
Ignore what God shows in The Great Commission.
When kids wonder if faith is only private, the Great Commission shows that good news is meant to be shared.
quiz_questions.answer: When kids wonder if faith is only private, the Great Commission shows that good news is meant to be shared.
quiz_questions.explanation: A useful Bible lesson changes how we see a real choice. Jesus sends His followers to make disciples and promises to be with them.

memory_verse.prompt: Read Matthew 28:20 again after the lesson and connect it to the story's main choice or promise.

discussion_questions: What surprised you in The Great Commission?
Why does mission matter in The Great Commission?
What would change if someone actually lived out the mission lesson in The Great Commission?

activity.title: World Mission Map
activity.instructions: Draw a map or globe and mark three places where people need to hear about Jesus.

prayer_prompt: Jesus, help me remember the truth in The Great Commission and live it with people around me.
